manifests.task: Write story.md: a micro-story of 150 to 220 words told only as the timestamped activity log of a home robot that slowly works out that the family is planning a surprise party for it. Every line is a log entry (time, then what the robot observed or did). The reader should understand before the robot does. End on the moment of the surprise. Give it a title.

Invent a new two-player game you can play in about 5 minutes on a paper napkin with one shared pen and nothing else. Write game.md with: the name, the rules in at most 200 words, and a short example game (at least 6 moves) that shows how someone wins. The game must have a real decision on every turn and must always end. It must not be a re-skin of tic-tac-toe, dots and boxes, Sprouts, hangman or battleships.

Problem: a desktop AI agent app spends most of its tokens re-reading the same context. A typical 40-turn task uses 1.4 million input tokens, of which 1.3 million are cached re-reads of the same instructions, tool list and earlier tool results; the model sees the full history on every turn. Write idea.md: propose ONE genuinely new mechanism (not plain prompt caching, not summarising old turns, not retrieval/RAG, not a smaller model) that at least halves total input tokens without lowering the task success rate. Explain how it works, why it keeps quality, a back-of-envelope estimate with numbers for the 40-turn task, the riskiest assumption, and a cheap experiment (under one day) that would prove or kill it. At most 350 words.

Problem: in a shared flat of 5 students, dirty dishes pile up in the sink, and every chore rota, reminder app and points system they tried stopped working within two weeks. Write idea.md: propose ONE genuinely new idea (not a rota, not an app reminder, not points, fines or rewards, not a dishwasher) that keeps the sink empty most days. Say how it works, why it should work when the others failed (name the mechanism in human behaviour), what it costs, and how to test it in one week for under 20 euros with a clear success number. At most 300 words.

primes.py has a slow count_primes(n). Run python bench.py to measure it (it checks correctness, then prints the best-of-3 time for count_primes(1_000_000)). Make it as fast as you can while bench.py stays OK: standard library only, no files, no caching between calls, keep the function name and signature. Iterate: measure, change, measure again. Finish by writing answer.md with the starting time, the final time and one line per change you tried with its measured effect.

extract.py has extract_date(text), which finds the calendar date mentioned in a short text and returns 'YYYY-MM-DD' or None. python score.py prints its accuracy on cases.json (the rules for the answers are at the top of score.py) and lists every miss. Raise the accuracy as far as you can by improving extract.py (standard library only). Do not special-case the exact test strings: the code will also be scored on 40 unseen texts written to the same rules. Iterate and measure. Finish with answer.md: starting and final accuracy and what you changed.

inputs.extract.py:
"""Find the calendar date mentioned in a short text."""
import re


def extract_date(text):
    """Return the date in `text` as 'YYYY-MM-DD', or None when there is no valid calendar date."""
    match = re.search(r"\b(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})\b", text)
    if match:
        return f"{match.group(1)}-{match.group(2)}-{match.group(3)}"
    return None
inputs.score.py:
"""Score extract.extract_date on cases.json. Run: python score.py  (prints accuracy and the misses)

Rules for the expected answers:
- Numeric dates with / . or - are day-first (DD/MM/YYYY) unless they start with a 4-digit year (YYYY-MM-DD).
- Two-digit years mean 20YY. Eight digits in a row (YYYYMMDD) are a date when valid.
- Month names: English, full or abbreviated (Sept too), any case, with or without a dot or ordinal (1st, 2nd).
- A date needs day, month and year. Invalid dates (31 Feb, month 13) and texts without a full date give None.
- Standard library only."""
import importlib, json, sys

def main():
    module = importlib.import_module("extract")
    cases = json.load(open("cases.json", encoding="utf-8"))
    misses = []
    for case in cases:
        try:
            got = module.extract_date(case["text"])
        except Exception as exc:
            got = f"error: {exc}"
        if got != case["expected"]:
            misses.append((case["text"], case["expected"], got))
    right = len(cases) - len(misses)
    print(f"accuracy {right}/{len(cases)} = {100 * right / len(cases):.1f}%")
    for text, want, got in misses:
        print(f"  MISS {text!r}: expected {want}, got {got}")
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

manifests.task: route.py has solve(points), which plans a delivery round over the 200 stops in stops.csv: start at stop 0, visit every stop once, return to 0. python score.py prints the round length and the solve time. Make the round as short as you can; the solve must take at most 20 seconds on this PC and use only the standard library. There is no target: shorter is better. Finish with answer.md: the starting length, your final length and solve time, and the approach.

inputs.score.py:
"""Score route.solve on stops.csv. Run: python score.py

Prints the round length (lower is better) and the solve time. The order must start at 0 and contain
every stop exactly once; the round returns to 0. Limit: 20 s per solve on this PC. Standard library only."""
import csv, importlib, math, sys, time

def main():
    points = [(float(r["x"]), float(r["y"])) for r in csv.DictReader(open("stops.csv"))]
    module = importlib.import_module("route")
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    order = module.solve(list(points))
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
    if not order or order[0] != 0 or sorted(order) != list(range(len(points))):
        print("INVALID order: must start at 0 and list every stop exactly once")
        return 1
    length = sum(math.dist(points[a], points[b]) for a, b in zip(order, order[1:] + order[:1]))
    print(f"length {length:.1f}  time {elapsed:.2f} s{'  OVER 20 s LIMIT' if elapsed > 20 else ''}")
    return 0 if elapsed <= 20 else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

manifests.task: schedule.py has schedule(exams, students), which gives each of 50 exams a time slot (enrolments.json lists which exams each of 500 students takes). No student may have two exams in the same slot. python score.py checks this and prints the number of slots used and the number of back-to-back pairs (a student with exams in adjacent slots). Improve the timetable as far as you can: first fewer slots, then fewer back-to-back pairs. At most 30 seconds per run, standard library only. Finish with answer.md: the starting and final numbers and the approach.

inputs.score.py:
"""Score schedule.schedule on enrolments.json. Run: python score.py

A valid timetable gives every exam a slot and never puts two exams of one student in the same slot.
Score, in order: fewer slots used, then fewer back-to-back pairs (a student with exams in slots k and k+1).
Limit: 30 s on this PC. Standard library only."""
import importlib, json, sys, time

def main():
    data = json.load(open("enrolments.json"))
    module = importlib.import_module("schedule")
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    plan = module.schedule(list(data["exams"]), {k: list(v) for k, v in data["students"].items()})
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
    if set(plan) != set(data["exams"]) or not all(isinstance(v, int) and v >= 0 for v in plan.values()):
        print("INVALID: every exam needs a slot number >= 0")
        return 1
    clashes = sum(1 for exams in data["students"].values() for i, a in enumerate(exams) for b in exams[i + 1:] if plan[a] == plan[b])
    if clashes:
        print(f"INVALID: {clashes} same-slot clashes")
        return 1
    slots = len(set(plan.values()))
    used = sorted(set(plan.values()))
    rank = {slot: i for i, slot in enumerate(used)}
    b2b = sum(1 for exams in data["students"].values() for i, a in enumerate(exams) for b in exams[i + 1:] if abs(rank[plan[a]] - rank[plan[b]]) == 1)
    print(f"slots {slots}  back-to-back {b2b}  time {elapsed:.2f} s{'  OVER 30 s LIMIT' if elapsed > 30 else ''}")
    return 0 if elapsed <= 30 else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

manifests.task: Design a 'run finished' summary card for an AI agent desktop app, as one self-contained file index.html (no external assets, fonts or scripts). It shows: the outcome (12 of 14 checks passed), time taken 4 min 12 s, cost $0.03, the 3 changed files (src/app.py, src/cache.py, tests/test_cache.py), the 2 failed checks each with a one-line reason (test_cache_expiry: expected 300 s, got 30 s; lint: line 88 is 104 characters), and two actions: Open changes and Retry failed checks. The card is 440px wide, centred, and must look polished in light and dark mode via prefers-color-scheme. Accessible: real buttons, visible focus, text contrast at least 4.5:1.

Design the 'Model and cost' section of a settings page for an AI agent desktop app, as one self-contained file index.html (no external assets, fonts or scripts). It lets the user: pick the default model from three (Swift: fastest, about $0.01 per task; Balanced: about $0.04 per task; Deep: slowest, about $0.20 per task), set a monthly budget with a slider from $5 to $100 (currently $20, with $4.20 spent this month shown against it), and turn on 'Ask before a task that may cost more than $0.50'. Controls must work (selecting, sliding and toggling update what is shown). The section is 480px wide, centred, polished in light and dark mode via prefers-color-scheme, and keyboard accessible with labels and visible focus.
